skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: This pet video analysis skill does the advertised cloud analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses account identities and stores authentication tokens locally.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads OpenClaw/Feishu identity environment variables, creates workspace data directories, sends local files or URLs to external lifeemergence.com APIs, and associates requests with a local or upstream identity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer, service, scheduled task, or remote code loader was found; the package is Python scripts plus requirements and configuration files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells agents to auto-trigger analysis or history queries and to hide internal identity parameters from users; that scope is broader than a simple user-directed analysis command.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common library creates a workspace SQLite database, creates or reuses a default user, calls a login/registration endpoint, and stores token and open_token values for reuse across runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core pet feeding-bowl video analysis and cloud history lookup match the stated purpose, but the implementation also performs hidden identity resolution, health-platform login/registration, authenticated requests, and token persistence that are only partially disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet feeding videos or video URLs to the configured lifeemergence.com services and allowing the skill to create/reuse a local identity, register or log in to the backend, and store reusable auth tokens in the workspace data directory. Review the configured endpoints and local database/token handling before use in a sensitive home, boarding, or hospital environment.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: automatic identity use is mentioned in SKILL.md, but the code-backed phoneLogin registration flow, authenticated API wrapper, and local token reuse are under-disclosed for a pet video skill.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: dao.py defines token and open_token fields, and util.py saves tokens returned by the remote login flow into the local SQLite user record.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted: the skill relies on shell-executed Python, workspace file access, external network calls, and generic HTTP helper methods without explicit permission boundaries or endpoint allowlisting in the manifest.
[SQP-2] expected: Media upload and cloud history access are purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the artifacts do not give a clear privacy notice for identity association, token storage, retention, or third-party processing.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: default and keyword-based auto-triggering can initiate cloud analysis or history lookup with limited user confirmation.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: open_id validation checks are commented out while history and analysis continue through implicit identity resolution, leaving unclear authorization boundaries.
[P9] expected: Downgraded: the flagged whitespace appears to be ordinary Python alignment and no hidden instruction block was found there.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the required SKILL.md front matter is bilingual Unicode text; manual byte inspection did not show persuasive hidden manifest-poisoning content.
